Two explicit trees of equal order eleven now share stronger degree-labelled radius-one and pairwise-distance invariants while producing exactly opposite cover-time changes. General cover-time formulas and constant-factor edge-addition inequalities do not supply this witness. value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work explicitly leaves the equality-of-order restriction outside its radius-dependent nonlocality examples. Resolving its natural first-radius same-order case via an exact small-tree witness, moreover preserving complete marked pairwise distances and effective resistance, identifies a substantive obstruction to predicting cover-time sensitivity from local information. The result does not require or claim a broader theorem.
